nora: Quick note: the Go generator sample leaks goroutines when the caller cancels mid-stream. Repro in the sample app: start generator, sleep a bit, cancel ctx, observe leftover goroutines (handshake reader blocked on ackCh).

ben: saw this too. repro reliable on mac and linux. likely that handshakeLoop doesn't exit on ctx.Done().

ashwin: can you drop the minimal snippet you used?

nora: yep. pared-down sample:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
iter := client.Generator(ctx, req)
go func() {
  time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)
  cancel()
}()
for iter.Next() {
  _ = iter.Token()
}
fmt.Println("iter err:", iter.Err())
```
After cancel the iterator stops yielding but pprof shows a goroutine stuck in generator.go:handshakeLoop waiting for ackCh.

chris: hmm. isn't there an existing close path for ackCh? wonder if there's a race where cancel happens before writer sets up.

dev-bot: Created issue #371: "go-sdk: generator ack channel goroutine leak on ctx cancel"  https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/issues/371

ben: potential fix: add a small watcher goroutine that waits on ctx.Done() and calls an idempotent cleanup that closes ackCh via sync.Once. avoids double-close.

ashwin: i'd prefer the writer owns the channel close and we signal the writer to stop. but i agree sync.Once makes that safe. alternative: make iterator implement io.Closer and call Close() in defer in samples. but we shouldn't force users to remember Close() in every simple example.

nora: onboarding-first principle: samples must work with plain ctx cancellation. but also show `defer iter.Close()` in advanced examples. we should add a ForEach helper too for one-off usage so users don't manage Next/Err boilerplate.

ben: ForEach(ctx, fn) makes sense. It would manage internal cleanup and respect ctx. i'll prototype it in the PR.

chris: add tests: unit test for handshake cleanup (ensures ackCh closed exactly once) and integration test that cancels after first token and asserts goroutine count returns within 200ms. we should run the integration in CI with the race detector off (flaky otherwise).

ashwin: also audit other handshake codepaths (dedicated/private runtime adapters) to ensure they use the same cleanup helpers. we don't want duplicate surface area.

nora: sample app update: shorten to a minimal example demonstrating cancel and also include ForEach usage. docs: short note on cancellation best practices and link to the issue/PR.

ben: i'll open a draft PR implementing sync.Once cleanup + io.Closer + ForEach helper. tests included. PR will reference #371.

dev-bot: Milestone set to v0.14.2. PR #482 draft opened by @ben referencing issue #371.

chris: one small API nit: ForEach should accept func(ctx context.Context, tok Token) error so user can early-return an error to stop iteration. ben: will do.

nora: perfect. once PR lands, i'll update the onboarding README and sample app in the docs repo.

ashwin: i'll review the PR and run a focused Dedicated runtime test.

ben: thanks team. i'll post the PR link here when ready.

chris: great. tagging follow-ups: ben -> PR, ashwin -> Dedicated audit, nora -> docs update. ping when green. :white_check_mark:
